title: When user selects an older Libreoffice Calc entry, it gets pasted as image into Libreoffice or browsers.
line: Picking an older LibreOffice Calc entry from the clipboard history now pastes the cells again instead of a picture or a paste error.
explanation: Klipper only stores text and image formats in its history, so it dropped LibreOffice's native formats when saving a Calc copy. When the entry was picked again, only the SVG/PNG pictures, HTML, RTF and plain text came back, so Calc pasted a picture of the cells (now it even fails with "The contents of the clipboard could not be pasted", because the SVG comes first). The change also stores the source's first (preferred) format, as Nate chose in the bug, plus LibreOffice's small object descriptor, without which Calc cannot paste its native format as cells.

commits.message:
klipper: keep the preferred format and LibreOffice's object descriptor

Klipper dropped LibreOffice's native formats, so a Calc entry picked
from the history pasted as a picture or not at all. Also keep the first
offered format and LibreOffice's object descriptor, which Calc needs.

BUG: 524503

media.caption: Pure master: after picking the older '1 2' Calc entry from the clipboard history, Ctrl+V in C1 shows 'The contents of the clipboard could not be pasted'.
With the fix, the same steps paste the cells 1 and 2 into C1:C2.

review.text: Well-investigated fix in Klipper that keeps the source's first offered MIME format (matching the option chosen in the bug discussion) plus LibreOffice's object descriptor so Calc restores actual cells rather than an embedded object, image, or paste error. Plain-text duplicates are properly excluded, the existing 20 MB limit still applies, and verification covers cross-process paste, database persistence across plasmashell restarts, Writer, and Dolphin. Minor nitpick: checking it == begin could miss the preferred format if a client places a non-MIME target without '/' at index 0.

reviews.text: Well-investigated fix in Klipper that keeps the source's first offered MIME format (matching the option chosen in the bug discussion) plus LibreOffice's object descriptor so Calc restores actual cells rather than an embedded object, image, or paste error. Plain-text duplicates are properly excluded, the existing 20 MB limit still applies, and verification covers cross-process paste, database persistence across plasmashell restarts, Writer, and Dolphin. Minor nitpick: checking it == begin could miss the preferred format if a client places a non-MIME target without '/' at index 0.

This implements the option the Klipper developer proposed and Nate approved in the bug: always store the source's first offered format. It adds LibreOffice's object descriptor, which the rig showed Calc needs to paste the native format as cells rather than as an embedded object. The paste was checked in a freshly started Calc and after a plasmashell restart, so it isn't Calc's internal clipboard (the marching ants show in both shots), and Writer, Dolphin and plain-text entries are unchanged. The existing 20 MB cap still applies to the newly kept format. The browser half of the title comes down to LibreOffice's own format order, which Klipper now reproduces like the original copy. The LibreOffice-specific descriptor line is a small, commented special case that a maintainer should accept.
